findings.title: ValidatorSanityChecker Has No Access Control on Setter Functions
findings.description: The ValidatorSanityChecker contract does not inherit from Ownable, AccessControl, or any access control framework. All four setter functions (setSlashingTolerance, setRewardsTolerance, setScoreTolerance, setMaxScoreBound) are bare external functions with no modifiers. Any address can call them to widen oracle validation tolerances up to their maximum values, completely neutering the protocol's only defense against oracle data manipulation for economic values.

findings.title: Single Oracle Compromise Enables Full Exchange Rate Control
findings.description: MIN_VALID_ORACLES is initialized to 1 in initialize(). The generatePerformance() function only requires validOracleCount >= MIN_VALID_ORACLES. With this default, a single oracle's data is accepted as ground truth with no cross-validation. A compromised oracle operator can report arbitrarily large accRewardAmount to inflate totalRewards and the exchange rate, draining funds, or inflate accSlashAmount to cause underflow and brick the protocol. Combined with missing access control on ValidatorSanityChecker, this creates a kill chain requiring no privileged roles beyond oracle operator.

findings.title: Decimal Mismatch in Exchange Rate Formula Breaks Reward Accrual
findings.description: The exchange rate formula mixes values of different decimal scales: totalStaked and totalClaimed are in 18 decimals (from msg.value and hypeAmount), while rewardsAmount and slashingAmount are in 8 decimals (from ValidatorManager, documented as 'In 8 decimals'). This means rewards and slashing are 10^10 times too small relative to stakes/claims, making a 1 HYPE reward (1e8) negligible against 1 HYPE staked (1e18). The protocol's core value proposition of liquid staking with reward accrual does not function.

findings.title: Exchange Rate Underflow Bricks Entire Protocol
findings.description: The subtraction totalStaked + rewardsAmount - totalClaimed - slashingAmount in _getExchangeRatio() will revert with arithmetic underflow in Solidity 0.8+ if totalClaimed + slashingAmount > totalStaked + rewardsAmount. This would brick ALL operations dependent on the exchange rate: stake(), queueWithdrawal(), and confirmWithdrawal(). Attack vector: widen sanity checker tolerances (no ACL), then oracle inflates totalSlashing via reportSlashingEvent(), causing permanent DoS. Even without manipulation, a large slashing event with mass withdrawals could trigger this naturally.

findings.title: Deauthorize Manager Permanently Inflates Exchange Rate for Remaining Users
findings.description: When a StakingManager is deauthorized, its kHYPE token is removed from _uniqueTokens (reducing the totalKHYPESupply denominator), but its contributions to totalStaked and totalClaimed remain in the numerator. This permanently inflates the exchange rate for remaining managers' users. Example: Manager A stakes 1000 HYPE, mints 1000 kHYPE. Manager B stakes 500 HYPE. After deauthorizing Manager A: ratio = 1500/500 = 3:1. Manager B's users can withdraw 3x their stake, draining the protocol. Requires DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE.

findings.title: Unbounded totalRewards Accumulation Enables Unlimited Exchange Rate Inflation
findings.description: totalRewards has no cap, no per-call limit, and is monotonically increasing with no decrement function. Each call to reportRewardEvent() adds amount to totalRewards without any upper bound check relative to total staked value. Combined with oracle compromise, this enables unbounded exchange rate inflation since totalRewards feeds directly into the exchange rate numerator.

findings.title: SanityChecker Defaults to address(0) Bypassing All Oracle Data Validation
findings.description: The sanityChecker state variable is never set in initialize() and defaults to address(0). Line 242 of OracleManager explicitly skips all sanity checks when unset. Additionally, setSanityChecker() allows setting it back to address(0) since there is no zero-address check. Until explicitly configured post-deployment, the oracle data pipeline has zero validation for economic values including rewards, slashing, and balance.

findings.title: No Upper Bound on Oracle-Reported Balance and Reward/Slashing Amounts
findings.description: The inline validation in generatePerformance() only checks performance scores against maxPerformanceBound. The balance, accRewardAmount, and accSlashAmount values from oracle reports have no ceiling within OracleManager. When sanityChecker is address(0) (the default state), these values pass through completely unchecked. This enables arbitrarily large reward/slashing reports that directly impact the exchange rate.

findings.title: Monotonically Increasing Rewards/Slashing With No On-Chain Correction Mechanism
findings.description: totalRewards and totalSlashing in ValidatorManager are monotonically increasing with no decrement or correction function. Once a single oracle attack inflates totalRewards, the damage persists permanently. In subsequent oracle update cycles, honest oracles reporting lower cumulative values cause the delta check (avgRewardAmount < previousRewards) to evaluate false, silently skipping the update. A single successful oracle manipulation permanently corrupts the exchange rate with no on-chain recovery path short of a contract upgrade.

findings.title: Cancel/Redelegate Race Condition Permanently Strands Funds in L1 Spot Balance
findings.description: When queueWithdrawal() is called, it immediately queues an L1 undelegation. When cancelWithdrawal() is later called by MANAGER_ROLE, it returns kHYPE to the user and increments _cancelledWithdrawalAmount, but does NOT remove the already-queued L1 operation. If redelegateWithdrawnHYPE() is called before processL1Operations() processes the original queued withdrawal, it zeroes _cancelledWithdrawalAmount and re-delegates via SpotDeposit. Later, processL1Operations() processes the original withdrawal—undelegating and moving funds to spot balance—with no corresponding _cancelledWithdrawalAmount to trigger a subsequent redelegation, permanently stranding funds.

findings.title: Near-Zero Exchange Ratio Enables Outsized kHYPE Minting Diluting Existing Holders
findings.description: If accumulated slashing drains totalHYPE to a near-zero value while totalKHYPESupply remains nonzero, the exchange ratio becomes extremely small. In HYPEToKHYPE(), Math.mulDiv(HYPEAmount, 1e18, nearZeroRatio) returns an astronomically large kHYPE amount for a small deposit. This is distinct from the underflow revert case—here the value doesn't underflow but approaches zero through legitimate accumulated slashing, producing a value extraction attack where new stakers acquire outsized protocol claims for minimal cost, completely diluting existing kHYPE holders.

findings.title: redelegateWithdrawnHYPE Omits recordStake Causing Progressive Exchange Rate Deflation
findings.description: When cancelWithdrawal() is followed by redelegateWithdrawnHYPE(), the HYPE is re-delegated via the SpotDeposit path in _distributeStake(). Unlike the UserDeposit path (which calls stakingAccountant.recordStake(msg.value)), the SpotDeposit path does NOT call recordStake(). The HYPE is re-staked on L1 but totalStaked is not incremented. After each cancel-redelegate cycle, the Accountant's totalStaked undercounts actual staked HYPE, progressively deflating the exchange rate with no self-correction mechanism.

findings.title: confirmWithdrawal Bypasses Withdrawal-Specific Pause Modifier
findings.description: confirmWithdrawal() uses the whenNotPaused modifier but not whenWithdrawalNotPaused. Users can confirm and drain funds from previously-queued requests even when withdrawal operations are specifically paused by the protocol. This undermines the intended security boundary of the withdrawal-specific pause mechanism.

findings.title: First Depositor Exchange Rate Inflation Attack via Missing Dead Shares
findings.description: The exchange rate starts at 1:1 when totalKHYPESupply == 0 with no virtual offset or dead shares mechanism. A first depositor could exploit this with very small stakes if combined with reward manipulation to inflate the exchange rate before other users join. Without a minimum initial stake requirement or dead shares minted to address(0), the protocol is vulnerable to the classic ERC4626 inflation attack.

findings.title: Zero Withdrawal Delay Allows Atomic Queue-Confirm Attacks
findings.description: setWithdrawalDelay() accepts zero with no minimum enforcement. With delay=0, same-block queue-and-confirm is possible, enabling flash loan attacks and atomic manipulation of the withdrawal flow. The lack of a minimum withdrawal delay (e.g., 1 hour) removes a critical temporal security boundary.

findings.title: Manager-Only cancelWithdrawal Creates Centralization Risk and State Inconsistency
findings.description: Only MANAGER_ROLE can cancel withdrawals; users cannot cancel their own pending requests. Additionally, cancellation does not remove the already-queued L1 undelegation operation, creating an inconsistency between L1 and EVM state. Users are dependent on a centralized role to cancel their withdrawals, and even when cancelled, L1 operations proceed regardless.

findings.title: processValidatorRedelegation Checks EVM Balance Instead of L1 Staking Balance
findings.description: processValidatorRedelegation() checks address(this).balance (EVM balance) as a guard, but the RebalanceDeposit operation acts on the L1 staking balance. These are semantically different quantities. The EVM balance check provides no meaningful guarantee about whether sufficient L1 staking balance exists for the redelegation operation.

findings.title: Oracle Reward Inflation Skews Exchange Rate Without Proportional kHYPE Minting
findings.description: Oracle manipulation can inflate totalRewards without proportional kHYPE minting, skewing the exchange rate in favor of existing holders who can then withdraw more HYPE than they deposited. Requires oracle cooperation or compromise. The 24-hour MIN_UPDATE_INTERVAL means oracle updates are batched and large, amplifying the impact of each manipulation.

findings.title: getDelegation Reverts on Inactive Validator Causing Stake and Withdraw DoS
findings.description: If the delegated validator is deactivated, getDelegation() reverts, blocking stake() and queueWithdrawal() for that StakingManager. No atomic deactivate-and-redelegate function exists, requiring a multi-step migration that may leave the manager non-functional during the transition window. Users cannot interact with a StakingManager assigned to a deactivated validator.

findings.title: Oracle-Controlled Balance Enables Sanity Check Bypass via Tolerance Scaling
findings.description: updateValidatorPerformance() accepts arbitrary balance values from the oracle. The ValidatorSanityChecker uses balance as the denominator for tolerance calculations, so inflating balance makes large reward/slashing increments appear within tolerance as a percentage. This allows a compromised oracle to first report an inflated balance to widen the effective tolerance, then report large reward/slashing increments that pass the sanity check.

findings.title: Silent Oracle Adapter Failures via try/catch Reduce Effective Oracle Count
findings.description: Oracle adapter failures in generatePerformance() are silently swallowed via try/catch with no event emitted. This reduces the effective oracle count without any notification or circuit breaker. A subset of oracles going offline or being compromised could silently reduce the quorum to a level controlled by an attacker without any on-chain visibility.

findings.title: Simple Mean Aggregation Allows Single Oracle Outlier to Shift Results
findings.description: generatePerformance() uses simple arithmetic mean aggregation for oracle data. This allows a single outlier oracle to shift the aggregate result by up to 1/N of its deviation from the true value. In a 3-oracle setup, one compromised oracle can move the aggregate by 33% of its manipulation. Median aggregation would provide complete outlier resistance with the same quorum.

findings.title: OPERATOR Role Can Disable Performance Score Validation via maxPerformanceBound
findings.description: The same OPERATOR role that executes generatePerformance() can also call setMaxPerformanceBound() to set maxPerformanceBound to type(uint256).max, effectively disabling score validation entirely. This violates the principle of least privilege as the operator role gains the ability to weaken its own validation constraints.

findings.title: Deauthorizing Contract While Paused Prevents Unpausing
findings.description: deauthorizeContract() removes a contract from authorization but does not clear its isPaused mapping entry. If a contract is paused and then deauthorized, unpauseContract() requires the caller to be authorized—creating a deadlock where the contract cannot be unpaused. Recovery requires re-authorizing the contract then unpausing it, which may not be possible if the contract was deauthorized for security reasons.

findings.title: KHYPE Token Pause Blocks Protocol Mint/Burn Preventing Emergency Withdrawals
findings.description: KHYPE._update() has a whenNotPaused modifier that blocks all ERC20 operations including the protocol's own mint and burn calls during a pause. This means users cannot unstake or complete withdrawals during an emergency pause of the KHYPE token, trapping user funds. Emergency withdrawal functionality should at minimum allow burn operations to proceed.

findings.title: DefaultOracle Lacks Monotonicity Enforcement on Cumulative Reward/Slashing Values
findings.description: The DefaultOracle's updateValidatorMetrics() accepts decreased cumulative reward or slashing values with no monotonicity validation. Since OracleManager computes deltas by comparing current to previous cumulative values, a non-monotonic report causes the delta check to evaluate to false, silently skipping a reporting cycle. This creates unpredictable behavior when oracle data is corrected or rolled back.

findings.title: resetL1OperationsQueue Enables Double-Processing of Already-Submitted L1 Operations
findings.description: resetL1OperationsQueue() deletes _pendingWithdrawals and _pendingDeposits arrays and resets processing indices to 0. However, L1 operations already submitted via processL1Operations() cannot be recalled. After a queue reset, the accounting (totalStaked, buffer tracking) has already been updated for processed operations. The deleted-but-processed entries still execute on L1, while new operations re-queued after the reset may overlap with in-flight L1 operations, causing double delegation or double undelegation.

findings.title: executeEmergencyWithdrawal Omits All Accounting Updates Creating State Discrepancy
findings.description: executeEmergencyWithdrawal() sends an L1 undelegation via l1Write.sendTokenDelegate() but does not call recordClaim() or update totalStaked, totalClaimed, totalQueuedWithdrawals, or any buffer tracking. The undelegated HYPE eventually returns to the contract but the exchange rate formula still counts it as staked. This creates a permanent discrepancy between actual L1 state and on-chain accounting that inflates the exchange rate.

findings.title: Missing Storage Gap in All Upgradeable Contracts Risks Storage Collision on Upgrade
findings.description: None of the upgradeable contracts (StakingManager, StakingAccountant, ValidatorManager, OracleManager, PauserRegistry, KHYPE) declare a __gap storage variable. Without storage gaps, adding new state variables in future upgrades could overwrite existing storage slots of child contracts. This is a well-known OpenZeppelin upgrade safety pattern that is absent throughout the codebase.

findings.title: Unbounded L1 Operation Queue Growth Enables Gas DoS on processL1Operations
findings.description: The _pendingWithdrawals and _pendingDeposits arrays grow unboundedly as users stake and withdraw. processL1Operations() iterates through these arrays. If the queue grows large enough, processing becomes impossible within block gas limits. While the batchSize parameter helps, the queue cannot be fully compacted—completed entries are tracked by index but not deleted, so the array grows indefinitely.

findings.title: Zero-HYPE Withdrawal Requests Permanently Lock kHYPE in Contract
findings.description: When queueWithdrawal(kHYPEAmount) is called with a small amount where fee deduction plus exchange rate conversion produces hypeAmount == 0, the withdrawal request is created but can never be confirmed (line 382 skips hypeAmount == 0 requests) and can never be cancelled (line 921 requires hypeAmount > 0). The kHYPE transferred during queue creation is permanently locked in the contract. Only kHYPEAmount > 0 is validated, not the post-fee hypeAmount.

findings.title: setTreasury Does Not Sync TREASURY_ROLE Leaving Old Address With Privileged Access
findings.description: setTreasury() updates the treasury state variable but does not revoke TREASURY_ROLE from the old address or grant it to the new one. After a treasury change: the old treasury retains TREASURY_ROLE and can call rescueToken() and withdrawTokenFromSpot(); the new treasury cannot call these role-gated functions; fee exemptions in queueWithdrawal() use the state variable correctly, but role-gated functions use stale AccessControl state.

findings.title: deauthorizeOracle Can Drop Active Oracle Count Below MIN_VALID_ORACLES Bricking Updates
findings.description: deauthorizeOracle() and setOracleActive(adapter, false) do not check whether removing or deactivating the oracle would leave fewer active oracles than MIN_VALID_ORACLES. If too many oracles are removed or deactivated, generatePerformance() always reverts at the 'Insufficient valid oracles' check, permanently preventing reward/slashing reporting and exchange rate updates.

findings.title: Deauthorizing StakingManager Traps Users With Pending Withdrawals
findings.description: When a StakingManager is deauthorized via deauthorizeStakingManager(), subsequent calls to recordClaim() from that manager revert with 'Not authorized'. Since confirmWithdrawal() calls recordClaim(), users with pending withdrawals in that manager can never confirm them. Their kHYPE is locked in the manager contract and their HYPE is trapped, with no emergency recovery mechanism.

findings.title: KHYPE.decimals() Returns 18 While Protocol NatSpec Assumes 8 Decimals
findings.description: KHYPE inherits the default ERC20 18-decimal decimals() function, but protocol NatSpec comments in StakingManager repeatedly describe kHYPE as '8 decimals'. Any external integration (DEX, wallet, frontend) querying decimals() will interpret kHYPE values as 18-decimal, displaying amounts that are 10^10 times larger or smaller than intended. This creates systematic integration failures.

findings.title: Oracle Set Changes Cause Silent Reward Under-Reporting via Averaging Artifact
findings.description: Oracle reports use cumulative accumulated values. generatePerformance() computes deltas by comparing averaged cumulative values to the previous report. If a new oracle is authorized with lower historical cumulative values, the average drops below the previously reported cumulative, causing avgRewardAmount < previousRewards. The if check evaluates to false and the legitimate reward delta is silently skipped. Adding oracles can paradoxically cause reward under-reporting.

findings.title: Front-Running Oracle Updates Enables MEV Extraction From Exchange Rate Changes
findings.description: Withdrawal hypeAmount is locked at queue-time exchange rate. Users monitoring the mempool for generatePerformance() calls that will report slashing can front-run by queuing withdrawals at the pre-slashing rate. The 24-hour MIN_UPDATE_INTERVAL means oracle updates are batched and large, amplifying extractable value per update cycle. Conversely, back-running reward events by staking immediately before the update captures the pre-reward rate.

findings.title: closeRebalanceRequests Can Consume HYPE Buffer Earmarked for User Withdrawals
findings.description: processValidatorRedelegation() checks address(this).balance >= amount but does not exclude hypeBuffer or pending withdrawal amounts from the available balance. A rebalance operation can consume HYPE intended for user withdrawal confirmations, causing subsequent confirmWithdrawal() calls to fail with insufficient contract balance. The available balance for rebalancing should exclude totalQueuedWithdrawals and hypeBuffer.

findings.title: setWithdrawalDelay Retroactively Affects All Pending Withdrawals Including Already-Queued
findings.description: withdrawalDelay is a global variable checked at confirmation time. Changing it affects all pending requests retroactively. Setting it to type(uint256).max permanently traps all queued funds; setting it to 0 enables atomic attacks on existing queued requests. Users queuing withdrawals cannot predict when their request will be confirmable, and the delay can be changed by admin after they commit.

findings.title: queueL1Operations Allows OPERATOR to Inject UserWithdrawal Type Bypassing Accounting
findings.description: queueL1Operations() allows OPERATOR_ROLE to queue any OperationType including UserWithdrawal, which triggers sendTokenDelegate (undelegation) AND sendCWithdrawal (staking to spot) when processed. This occurs without any corresponding user withdrawal request, totalQueuedWithdrawals update, or recordClaim() call. A compromised OPERATOR could move funds from staking to spot balance without accounting, then extract via withdrawFromSpot().

findings.title: Queued Withdrawal kHYPE Still Counted in totalSupply During Queue-to-Confirm Window
findings.description: Between queueWithdrawal() and confirmWithdrawal(), locked kHYPE is still counted in totalKHYPESupply while hypeAmount is fixed and totalClaimed has not yet increased. The exchange rate appears unchanged but the backing HYPE is committed. Rewards accruing during this window are socialized only to remaining non-withdrawing holders, creating incentive to front-run reward oracle updates by queuing withdrawals beforehand.

findings.title: Rounding Asymmetry in Rebalance Operations Causes Systematic Dust Leak Per Cycle
findings.description: Rebalance withdrawal uses _convertTo8Decimals(amount, true) which rounds UP for undelegation, but redelegation uses _convertTo8Decimals(amount, false) which rounds DOWN. For non-aligned amounts, exactly 1 unit in 8 decimals (= 1e10 wei) is undelegated but never redelegated per cycle. This systematically leaks funds from validator delegations to the L1 staking balance, untracked and unrecoverable.

findings.title: Staking Limit Uses Global totalRewards Without Per-Manager Accounting
findings.description: The staking limit calculation uses the global totalRewards value rather than per-manager reward contributions. This means that rewards generated by one StakingManager's validators reduce the available staking capacity for all other managers, creating unexpected cross-manager interactions and potentially preventing legitimate staking in some managers.

findings.title: Staking Limit Omits Slashing Amount Allowing Staking Beyond Safe Threshold
findings.description: The staking limit calculation does not include slashing amounts, meaning the maximum stake threshold does not account for value already lost to slashing. Slashing reduces the effective backing of kHYPE but does not reduce the staking limit denominator, potentially allowing more HYPE to be staked than can be safely backed.

findings.title: rescueToken Cannot Handle Native Token Despite Documentation Suggesting It Can
findings.description: rescueToken() is documented as a general token rescue function but cannot handle native HYPE tokens. Attempting to rescue accidentally sent native tokens will fail or behave unexpectedly. The documentation should be corrected or native token rescue functionality should be added.

findings.title: Rounding in _convertTo8Decimals Systematically Favors Users Over Protocol
findings.description: _convertTo8Decimals() rounds in a direction that systematically favors users when converting withdrawal amounts. While individually small, this creates a consistent 1-unit-per-transaction loss that accumulates over many operations. Consider whether rounding should favor the protocol for withdrawal amount conversions to prevent systematic value extraction.

findings.title: No Bounds on recordClaim Allowing totalClaimed to Theoretically Exceed totalStaked
findings.description: recordClaim() has no invariant check that totalClaimed remains bounded by totalStaked plus rewards. If called incorrectly or through a compromised manager, totalClaimed could exceed the total backing, causing the exchange rate formula to underflow or return incorrect values. A safety invariant should ensure totalClaimed never exceeds totalStaked plus rewards.

findings.title: External Calls to Potentially Untrusted kHYPE Token Contracts Without Validation
findings.description: StakingManager makes external calls to kHYPE token contracts without validating that they conform to the expected interface beyond the call itself. A malicious or buggy kHYPE token could cause unexpected behavior during mint/burn operations. Token contracts should be validated at registration time.

findings.title: Access Control Asymmetry Between authorizeStakingManager and deauthorizeStakingManager
findings.description: authorizeStakingManager() and deauthorizeStakingManager() use different roles, creating an asymmetry where one role can authorize but cannot deauthorize and vice versa. This could lead to operational issues where authorized managers cannot be removed by the expected role, requiring coordination between different role holders.

findings.title: Latent Validator Array Index Inconsistency in Parallel Storage Structures
findings.description: ValidatorManager uses parallel arrays for validator storage, creating risk of index inconsistency if array operations are not perfectly synchronized. Using a mapping instead of parallel arrays would eliminate this class of bug entirely and provide O(1) lookups without index management complexity.

findings.title: Unbounded Validator Storage Growth Risks Gas Exhaustion on Iteration
findings.description: ValidatorManager has no mechanism to remove validators from storage. As validators are added over time, the validator array grows unboundedly. Operations that iterate over all validators will eventually exceed block gas limits, creating a long-term denial of service risk for validator management operations.

findings.title: Missing whenNotPaused on reportRewardEvent and reportSlashingEvent
findings.description: reportRewardEvent() and reportSlashingEvent() lack whenNotPaused modifiers. During a protocol pause intended to halt operations, these functions continue to modify totalRewards and totalSlashing, potentially allowing continued oracle manipulation even when the protocol is in an emergency paused state.

findings.title: Oracle Staleness Check Relies on Self-Attested Timestamp From Oracle
findings.description: The DefaultOracle staleness check uses a timestamp field provided by the oracle itself rather than tracking when the OracleManager last received the data. A compromised or buggy oracle could submit stale data with a current timestamp, bypassing the staleness check entirely. Timestamps should be recorded by the OracleManager upon receipt.

findings.title: maxScoreBound Has No Upper Limit in ValidatorSanityChecker
findings.description: setMaxScoreBound() in ValidatorSanityChecker accepts any value greater than 0 with no upper bound. Setting maxScoreBound to an arbitrarily large value effectively disables the score bound check since all reported scores will be within bounds. An upper limit of BASIS_POINTS or similar should be enforced.

findings.title: batchConfirmWithdrawals Silently Skips Invalid and Early Withdrawals
findings.description: batchConfirmWithdrawals() iterates through withdrawal IDs and silently skips requests that are invalid or not yet past the withdrawal delay. Callers receive no indication of which withdrawals were skipped or why. The function should either revert on invalid IDs or emit events for skipped withdrawals to enable proper off-chain monitoring.

findings.title: No Minimum Withdrawal Amount Allows Dust Withdrawals Wasting Gas and State
findings.description: queueWithdrawal() only validates that kHYPEAmount > 0 with no minimum threshold. Users can create withdrawal requests for tiny amounts that produce negligible hypeAmount values after fee deduction and exchange rate conversion. This wastes gas, pollutes storage, and creates potential edge cases where post-fee hypeAmount is zero.

findings.title: receive() Delegates to Complex stake() Failing With Low-Gas transfer and send
findings.description: The receive() fallback function calls the complex stake() function which requires significantly more than the 2300 gas stipend provided by transfer() and send(). Any integration or user attempting to stake via simple ETH transfer will fail, while direct call() transactions will work. This creates inconsistent behavior depending on the transfer method used.

findings.title: Treasury Address Change Can DoS Pending Withdrawal Confirmations
findings.description: If the treasury address changes between queueWithdrawal() and confirmWithdrawal(), the fee calculation path in confirmWithdrawal() may fail or behave unexpectedly for pending withdrawals that assumed the original treasury. This creates a potential DoS vector where a treasury change blocks confirmation of already-queued withdrawals.

findings.title: withdrawFromSpot Has No Accounting Integration With Buffer or totalStaked
findings.description: withdrawFromSpot() moves funds from L1 spot balance back to the contract but does not update hypeBuffer, totalStaked, or any other accounting variable. The exchange rate formula uses stale accounting values that no longer reflect actual L1 state after a spot withdrawal, creating a discrepancy between on-chain accounting and actual fund locations.

findings.title: SpotDeposit Path Loses 18-to-8 Decimal Remainder Unlike UserDeposit Path
findings.description: The SpotDeposit path in _distributeStake() loses the remainder from 18-to-8 decimal conversion without adding it to the buffer, unlike the UserDeposit path which adds the remainder to hypeBuffer. Over many SpotDeposit operations, the cumulative remainder loss creates a systematic accounting discrepancy between tracked and actual HYPE amounts.

findings.title: Withdrawal Whitelist Not Enforced on confirmWithdrawal and batchConfirmWithdrawals
findings.description: The protocol has a whitelist mechanism for controlling which addresses can interact, but this whitelist check is not enforced on confirmWithdrawal() and batchConfirmWithdrawals(). This creates an inconsistency where non-whitelisted users who somehow obtained a withdrawal request could still confirm it.

findings.title: deauthorizeContract Does Not Clear isPaused Mapping Causing Stale State Inheritance
findings.description: When a contract is deauthorized via deauthorizeContract() in PauserRegistry, its isPaused status is not cleared. If the same contract is later re-authorized, it inherits the stale paused state from before deauthorization. This could leave a re-authorized contract in an unexpected paused state without any explicit pause action having occurred.

findings.title: processL1Operations Lacks nonReentrant Modifier Despite External Calls to l1Write
findings.description: processL1Operations() makes multiple external calls to the l1Write contract without a nonReentrant guard. While l1Write is likely trusted, the absence of reentrancy protection means a compromised or upgraded l1Write contract could reenter processL1Operations() during execution, potentially causing double-processing of operations or state corruption.

findings.title: stake() Calls recordStake After Mint and External Calls Creating Transient Inconsistency
findings.description: In stake(), recordStake() is called after kHYPE is minted and after external calls are made. During this window, totalStaked understates the actual staked amount, creating a transient state inconsistency. If any external call reads the exchange rate during this window, it will see an incorrect value. recordStake() should be called before mint() or immediately after the amount is locked.

findings.title: withdrawFromSpot Missing whenNotPaused Allowing OPERATOR to Move Funds During Emergency
findings.description: withdrawFromSpot() lacks the whenNotPaused modifier, allowing OPERATOR_ROLE to move funds from L1 spot balance to the contract even during an emergency protocol pause. This undermines the security guarantee of the pause mechanism and could enable fund extraction during an emergency that was intended to freeze all operations.

findings.title: DefaultAdapter Is Pure Pass-Through With No Adapter-Level Validation
findings.description: DefaultAdapter is a pure pass-through that forwards oracle data without any adapter-level bounds checking or staleness validation. The adapter pattern suggests a location where per-source validation could be applied, but the DefaultAdapter provides no additional safety guarantees beyond what the underlying oracle provides.

findings.title: Score Change Checks Bypassed for New Validators With Zero Previous Score
findings.description: ValidatorSanityChecker's score change validation compares the new score against the previous score, but for new validators with a previous score of zero, any score passes the percentage-based change check since the delta relative to zero is effectively unconstrained. An initial baseline or separate validation for first-time validators should be applied.

findings.title: No emergencyUnpauseAll Counterpart to emergencyPauseAll in PauserRegistry
findings.description: PauserRegistry provides an emergencyPauseAll() function for rapid global pause, but no corresponding emergencyUnpauseAll() function exists. After an emergency pause, each contract must be unpaused individually, increasing recovery time during an incident. An authorized emergency role should be able to unpause all contracts atomically.

findings.title: Cross-Manager Subsidization via Shared Exchange Rate Is Architectural Design Issue
findings.description: The shared exchange rate across all StakingManagers means that rewards earned by one manager's validators benefit all kHYPE holders across all managers, and slashing in one manager affects all. This cross-subsidization may be intentional by design but creates unexpected economic coupling between otherwise independent staking managers.

findings.title: Exchange Rate Can Be Driven to Zero Through Accumulated Slashing Edge Case
findings.description: If accumulated slashing equals or exceeds totalStaked plus rewards, the exchange rate formula returns zero or causes underflow. While the underflow-revert case is covered in H-02, if a floor of zero is returned instead, subsequent staking operations would mint infinite kHYPE for any deposit amount. This edge case of H-02 may manifest differently depending on implementation of the underflow protection.

findings.title: Arbitrary stakingManager Address Parameter in rebalanceWithdrawal Not Validated
findings.description: rebalanceWithdrawal() accepts an arbitrary stakingManager address parameter that is passed to closeRebalanceRequests(). While restricted to MANAGER_ROLE, the absence of validation that the provided address is an authorized StakingManager creates a code quality issue and potential for operational mistakes.

findings.title: Inconsistent Access Control Pattern in deactivateValidator
findings.description: deactivateValidator() uses a different access control pattern compared to other validator management functions, creating an inconsistent security model. This inconsistency makes the access control requirements harder to audit and reason about, and may lead to operational confusion about which roles can perform which actions.

findings.title: closeRebalanceRequests Inherits Arbitrary stakingManager Risk From rebalanceWithdrawal
findings.description: closeRebalanceRequests() in StakingManager is called with an arbitrary stakingManager address from rebalanceWithdrawal(). The function trusts this parameter without verifying it is an authorized contract. While restricted to MANAGER_ROLE, the inherited risk from the calling context should be documented or validated.

findings.title: No Reentrancy Guard on generatePerformance Despite Multiple External Calls
findings.description: generatePerformance() makes multiple external calls to oracle adapters and ValidatorManager without a nonReentrant guard. While the function is access-controlled to OPERATOR_ROLE, the absence of reentrancy protection means a compromised oracle adapter could potentially reenter the function, causing duplicate reward/slashing reporting.

findings.title: withdrawTokenFromSpot Silently Returns on HYPE Token ID Without Event or Revert
findings.description: withdrawTokenFromSpot() silently returns when called with the HYPE token ID without performing any action and without emitting an event or reverting. This silent no-op behavior is confusing for callers who expect either a successful withdrawal or an explicit error, and prevents off-chain monitoring from detecting failed withdrawal attempts.
